title: Acute Cholecystitis
scenario: A 44-year-old female presents to the emergency department with severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain that began after a fatty meal and has persisted for several hours, radiating to the right shoulder.

lines: 44-year-old female presents with 6 hours of steady, severe right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder, worse after eating fried food. Reports nausea and two episodes of vomiting. Positive Murphy's sign on palpation. Guarding noted over the RUQ. Skin warm. Alert and oriented x3.
IV access established. Labs, abdominal ultrasound, and blood cultures ordered. Placed NPO. Antiemetic requested for nausea.
Ultrasound reports gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and multiple gallstones with a positive sonographic Murphy's sign. Surgical consult notified.
IV fluids infusing, IV antibiotic and analgesia administered per order. NG tube not required at this time. Client resting, pain reduced.
Reports pain now 3/10 from 9/10. No further vomiting. Tolerating NPO status. Afebrile. Awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the morning.
Acetaminophen 500 mg PO as needed for pain
Start IV isotonic fluids at 125 mL/hr
Administer IV ketorolac 15 mg for pain
Antiemetic ondansetron 4 mg IV for nausea
Notify provider for temperature above 102 F or worsening pain

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which 4 findings are consistent with acute cholecystitis and require follow-up?

options.text: Right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder

children.rationale: RUQ pain radiating to the shoulder, a positive Murphy's sign, fever, and leukocytosis together point to gallbladder inflammation. Normal oxygenation and intact orientation are expected findings.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects inflammation/infection, biliary obstruction, or both. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: Leukocytosis and fever indicate inflammation and infection. Elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase indicate obstruction of bile flow. Wall thickening with obstructing stones reflects both processes.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the immediate nursing goal is to {2}.

choices.text: acute pain with risk of infection from gallbladder inflammation
relieve pain and control infection while keeping the client NPO

children.rationale: The immediate threat is severe pain with an infected, inflamed gallbladder; the nurse prioritizes pain relief, antibiotics, and NPO status to rest the gallbladder before surgery.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Provide a high-fat meal to test tolerance
Apply firm deep pressure to the RUQ every hour

children.rationale: NPO rest, antibiotics, and analgesia treat cholecystitis. Fatty food triggers gallbladder contraction and pain, and repeated deep RUQ palpation is unnecessary and harmful; both are contraindicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which actions should the nurse take now based on the orders? Select all that apply.

options.text: Administer the IV antibiotic as ordered
Infuse IV isotonic fluids at 125 mL/hr
Offer a full oral diet immediately

children.rationale: NPO status, antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, and analgesia are the ordered priority actions to stabilize the client before cholecystectomy. Oral feeding and delaying antibiotics are not appropriate.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Reduced pain, resolving fever, normalizing pulse, and cessation of vomiting show the inflammation and infection are responding. Rising fever and worsening guarding would signal deterioration.
